rv.q: Both actors give engaging and nuanced performances.
Shifters may be a very small play but it strikes a symphony of resonant chords.

The two-person play, imported from the West End to A24’s Cherry Lane Theatre, is a love story told through its pivotal moments—if those moments were tossed in a raffle drum and plucked out one by one.
The grounded, open-hearted performances, under Linton's direction, make us lean in to learn more, to know these people better.
Ms. Lombe's one-act play offers glimmers of insight, along with some platitudes, and Ms. Linton and her players deliver them with grace and charm.
She attempts this in various ways, some more successful than others.

cn.t: Benedict Lombe's intimate two-hander earns praise for its universal meditation on love found and lost, elevated by the convincing chemistry and precise performances of Heather Agyepong and Daniel Ezra.
